To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GCN4-binding DNA has a bent, curved conformation and that the dynamics of the DNA molecule are sequence-dependent and have been correlated with recognition by the GCN4 protein.
the GCN4-binding site of the ATF/CREB transcription factor DNA is a curved DNA and that it is flexible in the free state, and that the dynamics of the DNA are sequence dependent.
the structure and the dynamics of GCN-4 cognate DNA have been determined by NMR and that these features of the molecule have a bearing on recognition by GCN-4 protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and dynamics, in solution, of DNA sequences that have been implicated in protein recognition.
the structure and dynamics (13)C NMR relaxation) of a 12 bp long DNA sequence, which is the cognate DNA sequence of a leucine zipper protein (GCN4) from yeast.
the structural and dynamic characterization of DNA molecules and their complexes in solution by NMR spectroscopic methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GCN4 protein binds to DNA in a sequence-dependent way and that the DNA is bent by 30 degrees in the complex with the protein.
the GCN4 protein binds to DNA with a sequence-specific recognition and the binding is accompanied by a conformational change of the DNA.
the DNA is curved in its free state and that this curvature is a significant determinant in recognition of the molecule by GCN4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DNA is highly dynamic and the dynamics are sequence-dependent.
the DNA structure and dynamics in solution are in good agreement with the X-ray data for the complex, which suggests that the DNA in solution is a good model for the complex.
the NMR structure of GCN4 DNA in solution is very similar to its X-ray structure in the complex with the DNA-binding domain of GCN4.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNA is highly mobile in solution.
the DNA is not a rigid molecule but is highly dynamic and that this dynamic behaviour has a significant bearing not only on the structure but also on the recognition of the DNA molecule by proteins.

GCN4 cognates are curved in the free form and the curvature is a significant factor in protein-DNA recognition.
